records.source: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῖς ἐν Κολοσσαῖς ἁγίοις καὶ πιστοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy the brother, \v 2 to the in Colossae holy [ones] and faithful brothers in Christ: grace to you and peace from God Father of us.
pieces: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, and from Timothy our brother,
to God's holy people in Colossae, the faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Grace and peace to you from God our Father.

L.1: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy [our] brother,
L.2: to the holy and faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [who are] in Colossae: grace to you and peace from God our Father.

R.1: This letter is from Paul and from our brother Timothy. It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
R.2: We are writing to God's holy people in the town of Colossae, our faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. May God our Father show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.choice: apostle: a messenger sent out with the authority of the one who sends him
alternatives: a missionary or church worker in general
decisions.reason: ἀπόστολος means one who is sent. Paul uses it for those commissioned by the risen Christ to speak for him, and counts himself among them (1 Corinthians 15:7-9; Galatians 1:1). He holds the role "through the will of God", not by any human choice.

decisions.choice: one group, described two ways: God's holy people, who are also faithful brothers and sisters in Christ
alternatives: two groups: the holy ones, and the faithful brothers
decisions.reason: One article, τοῖς, covers the whole phrase, so ἁγίοις and ἀδελφοῖς describe the same people. ἁγίοις can be an adjective with ἀδελφοῖς ("holy and faithful brothers") or Paul's usual word for believers as God's holy people (Philippians 1:1); either way the whole church is meant. ἀδελφοῖς is masculine plural, the ordinary way to address a group of men and women together.

decisions.choice: faithful: trustworthy and loyal to Christ
decisions.reason: πιστοῖς can mean "believing" or "faithful". Paul is not singling out the loyal few; he greets the whole church as people who are true to Christ, and the letter goes on to urge them to stay that way against teaching that would draw them off (2:4-8).

decisions.choice: Colossae: a small town in the Lycus valley, in the Roman province of Asia
decisions.reason: The letter names the two neighboring towns, Laodicea and Hierapolis (2:1; 4:13). Paul had not visited the church himself (2:1); the gospel had reached the town through Epaphras (1:7).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "from God our Father", without "and the Lord Jesus Christ"
alternatives: "from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and the Lord Jesus Christ", the wording of Paul's other greetings (Philippians 1:2). Important early manuscripts have the shorter text, and a copyist is more likely to have added the familiar words than to have dropped them. The meaning of the greeting is not changed.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus; in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is written to the whole church, women and men (4:15 greets Nympha and the church in her house). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: God's holy people
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
alternatives: an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what an apostle is and turns the opening of the letter into ordinary sentences, as Philippians 1:1 does.

decisions.choice: May God our Father show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God our Father
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as Philippians 1:2 does.

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: Εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ πατρὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι, ἀκούσαντες τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ἣν ἔχετε εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους διὰ τὴν ἐλπίδα τὴν ἀποκειμένην ὑμῖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ἣν προηκούσατε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ παρόντος εἰς ὑμᾶς, καθὼς καὶ ἐν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον καθὼς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐπέγνωτε τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ· καθὼς ἐμάθετε ἀπὸ Ἐπαφρᾶ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ συνδούλου ἡμῶν, ὅς ἐστιν πιστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν διάκονος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ καὶ δηλώσας ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἀγάπην ἐν πνεύματι.
records.gloss: We give thanks to the God Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ always concerning you praying, \v 4 having heard of the faith of you in Christ Jesus and the love which you have toward all the holy [ones] \v 5 because of the hope the [one] being laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard of before in the word of the truth of the gospel \v 6 the [one] being present to you, just as also in all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, just as also among you, from which day you heard and came to know the grace of the God in truth; \v 7 just as you learned from Epaphras the beloved fellow slave of us, who is faithful on behalf of us servant of the Christ, \v 8 the [one] also having made known to us the of you love in [the] Spirit.
pieces: Every time we pray for you, we give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}},
because we have heard of your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and of the love you have for all God's holy people.
That faith and love spring from the hope kept safe for you in heaven, the hope you first heard about in the message of truth, the gospel
that has reached you. All over the world this gospel is bearing fruit and growing, and it has done the same among you from the day you heard it and came to know God's grace in all its truth.
You learned it from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant, who serves {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} faithfully on our behalf.
He is also the one who told us about your love in the Spirit.

L.3: We give thanks to God, [the] Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, always, when praying for you,
L.4: since we heard of your faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus and of the love that you have for all the holy ones
L.5: because of the hope that is laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard of before in the word of the truth of the gospel
L.6: that has come to you, just as in all the world also it is bearing fruit and growing, as [it is] also among you, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
L.7: just as you learned [it] from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} on our behalf,
L.8: who also made known to us your love in [the] Spirit.

R.3: Every time we pray for you, we thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.4: We have heard about your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and the love you have for all of God's people.
R.5: Your faith and love come from what you hope for, which God is keeping safe for you in heaven. You first heard about this hope when the message of truth, the good news,
R.6: came to you. This good news is bearing fruit and growing all over the world. It has done the same among you, ever since the day you heard it and understood the truth about God's grace.
R.7: You learned it from Epaphras. He is our dear fellow servant: like us, he belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He serves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} faithfully in our place.
R.8: It was Epaphras who told us about the love the Spirit has given you.

decisions.choice: verses 3-8 are one sentence
alternatives: verse 7 begins a new sentence, as the SBLGNT's raised dot allows
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot at the end of verse 6, but verse 7 opens with καθὼς ("just as") and says where the Colossians learned the grace of God they came to know in verse 6, so it cannot stand on its own. The record keeps verses 3-8 together, as Philippians 1:3-7 does; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: "always" goes with giving thanks: every time they pray, they give thanks
alternatives: "always" goes with praying: we give thanks, praying for you always
decisions.reason: πάντοτε stands between the verb and the participle and could go with either. In Paul's other thanksgivings "always" goes with the thanks (1 Corinthians 1:4; 1 Thessalonians 1:2), and the sense is much the same: thanks rises whenever they pray.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God the Father"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here, and many read "God and Father". The SBLGNT has the two nouns side by side. All the readings say that the God they thank is the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ.

decisions.choice: the hope is the ground of their faith and love
alternatives: the hope is a further reason for Paul's thanks
decisions.reason: διὰ ("because of") stands nearer to faith and love than to "we give thanks", and Paul joins faith, love and hope elsewhere (1 Corinthians 13:13; 1 Thessalonians 1:3). They trust Christ and love his people because of what God has kept for them.

decisions.choice: hope: the thing hoped for, kept safe in heaven
alternatives: hope: the feeling or attitude of hoping
decisions.reason: A hope that is ἀποκειμένην ("laid up, stored away") is something real kept in store, like an inheritance (1 Peter 1:4). In verse 27 Paul names it: Christ in them, the hope of glory.

decisions.choice: the word of truth, which is the gospel
alternatives: the true word that belongs to the gospel
decisions.reason: The genitives explain one another: the message is "the truth", and that message is the gospel. Paul stresses that what they first heard was true before he warns them about teaching that is not (2:4, 2:8).

decisions.choice: bearing fruit and growing: perhaps an echo of God's first blessing on humankind, "be fruitful and multiply"
alternatives: a simple picture of growth, with no echo
decisions.reason: The pair may recall Genesis 1:28, where God blesses humankind to be fruitful and increase; the gospel now makes a new humanity grow across the world (compare 3:10). The words are not quoted exactly, so the echo is possible, not certain. Paul uses the same pair of the believers themselves in verse 10.

decisions.choice: in truth: they came to know God's grace as it really is
alternatives: truly, sincerely: they really did come to know it
decisions.reason: ἐν ἀληθείᾳ could describe their knowing (they truly knew it) or what they knew (grace in its truth, the true gospel). With "the word of the truth" in verse 5 and Epaphras's faithful teaching in verse 7, Paul's point is that they received the real gospel.

decisions.choice: Epaphras: a Colossian, through whom they first heard the gospel
decisions.reason: Epaphras is "one of you" (4:12) and taught them the gospel. He is now with Paul (4:12-13; Philemon 23). The name is a short form of Epaphroditus, but nothing connects him with the Epaphroditus of Philippians 2:25.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "on our behalf"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "on your behalf"; in Greek the two words differ by a single letter. With "on our behalf", Epaphras works in Colossae as Paul's representative. With "on your behalf", he serves Christ for the Colossians' good, as in 4:12-13. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves another, here Christ
decisions.reason: διάκονος is the general word for someone who serves (in Philippians 1:1 it names a group in the church). Paul uses it of himself as servant of the gospel (verse 23) and of the church (verse 25).

decisions.choice: love that the Spirit produces
alternatives: spiritual love, as opposed to physical
decisions.reason: πνεύματι most likely means the Holy Spirit, who gives love (Galatians 5:22; Romans 15:30). This is the only place in the letter where the Spirit is named.

decisions.choice: fellow slave: one who belongs, as Paul does, to the same master, Christ
decisions.reason: συνδούλου joins "with" to the word for a slave. Paul calls himself and Timothy slaves of Christ (Philippians 1:1), people who belong wholly to him; Epaphras belongs to the same master. He uses the same word of Tychicus in 4:7, and calls Epaphras "a slave of Christ Jesus" in 4:12.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article in verse 7: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: fellow servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m13) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave". Readable adds what it means: like Paul, he belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: Every time we pray for you, we give thanks
alternatives: We give thanks ..., always praying for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the prayer first, so that "always" is plainly about the thanks (m2).

decisions.choice: That faith and love spring from the hope (B); Your faith and love come from what you hope for (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "because of the hope" is tied to (m4).

decisions.choice: the love the Spirit has given you
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m12.

records.heading: Thanks for their faith and love

records.source: Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς, ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσαμεν, οὐ παυόμεθα ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι καὶ αἰτούμενοι ἵνα πληρωθῆτε τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ συνέσει πνευματικῇ, περιπατῆσαι ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου εἰς πᾶσαν ἀρεσκείαν ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ καρποφοροῦντες καὶ αὐξανόμενοι τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει δυναμούμενοι κατὰ τὸ κράτος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν ὑπομονὴν καὶ μακροθυμίαν μετὰ χαρᾶς, εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ πατρὶ τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν μερίδα τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί, ὃς ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ σκότους καὶ μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν·
records.gloss: Because of this also we, from which day we heard, do not cease on behalf of you praying and asking that you may be filled [with] the knowledge of the will of him in all wisdom and understanding spiritual, \v 10 to walk worthily of the Lord unto all pleasing, in every work good bearing fruit and growing in the knowledge of the God, \v 11 with all power being empowered according to the might of the glory of him unto all endurance and patience with joy, \v 12 giving thanks to the Father, the [one] having qualified you for the share of the lot of the holy [ones] in the light, \v 13 who rescued us out of the authority of the darkness and transferred [us] into the kingdom of the Son of the love of him, \v 14 in whom we have the redemption, the forgiveness of the sins.
pieces: That is why, from the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask God to fill you with the knowledge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, with all the wisdom and understanding the Spirit gives,
so that you may live in a way worthy of the Lord and please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in every way, bearing fruit in every kind of good work and growing in the knowledge of God.
We ask that you be made strong with all power by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious might, so that you may endure everything with patience and joy,
and give thanks to the Father, who has made you fit to share in the inheritance of God's holy people in the light.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of the Son {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves.
In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have redemption, which is the forgiveness of our sins.

L.9: Because of this we also, from the day we heard, do not stop praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
L.10: to walk worthily of the Lord, to please [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
L.11: being made strong with all power according to the might of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory for all endurance and patience with joy,
L.12: giving thanks to the Father, who qualified you for [your] share of the inheritance of the holy ones in the light,
L.13: who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred [us] into the kingdom of the Son of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love,
L.14: in whom we have the redemption, the forgiveness of sins.

R.9: So ever since we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask God to help you understand fully what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, and to give you all the wisdom and understanding that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit gives.
R.10: Then you will live in a way that honors the Lord and pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in everything. Your lives will bear fruit as you do every kind of good work, and you will keep growing in knowing God.
R.11: We pray that God will make you strong with all the power of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, so that you can keep going and stay patient whatever happens, and do it with joy.
R.12: And you will thank the Father, who has made you fit to receive your share of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people in the kingdom of light.
R.13: God has rescued us from the power of darkness and has brought us into the kingdom of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves.
R.14: Through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son we have been set free: our sins are forgiven.

decisions.choice: because of this: because of the faith, love and hope they have heard about (verses 4-8)
decisions.reason: Διὰ τοῦτο looks back to the report Epaphras brought. "From the day we heard" echoes "from the day you heard" in verse 6: since the day the gospel reached Colossae, and since the day the news of it reached Paul, prayer has not stopped.

decisions.choice: knowledge: a real grasp of God's will that shapes how one lives
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is a strengthened word for knowing, used for knowledge that grasps its object (Philippians 1:9). Here it is knowledge of God's will, and verse 10 says at once what it is for: a life that pleases the Lord. Knowledge and wisdom come up again and again in the letter (2:2-3; 3:10).

decisions.choice: spiritual: given by the Spirit
alternatives: spiritual as opposed to practical or worldly
decisions.reason: πνευματικῇ qualifies both wisdom and understanding. For Paul what is "spiritual" comes from God's Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:12-14), in contrast to wisdom that is merely human (2:8, 2:23).

decisions.choice: to walk: the purpose of being filled with knowledge is a life that pleases the Lord
alternatives: a second request alongside the first
decisions.reason: The infinitive περιπατῆσαι gives the purpose or result of the prayer in verse 9. "Walk" is a common biblical picture for the way a person lives (Philippians 3:17).

decisions.choice: four participles describe the worthy life: bearing fruit, growing, being strengthened, giving thanks
alternatives: "giving thanks" is Paul's own thanks, not part of his prayer for them
decisions.reason: Each participle is plural and agrees with "you", so all four describe the Colossians' life. Even "giving thanks" in verse 12 is part of what Paul prays for them, not a new thanksgiving of his own.

decisions.choice: growing in the knowledge of God
alternatives: growing by the knowledge of God
decisions.reason: The dative ἐπιγνώσει, without a preposition, can say in what they grow or by what. The two belong together: they grow in knowing God, and knowing God makes them grow. The sense "in" matches verse 9, where knowledge is what they are filled with.

decisions.choice: the might of his glory: his glorious power
alternatives: the might shown in his glory
decisions.reason: δόξης describes κράτος. God's glory is the shining greatness of who he is, and his might comes from it.

decisions.choice: "with joy" goes with endurance and patience
alternatives: "with joy" goes with giving thanks: "joyfully giving thanks"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after χαρᾶς, so joy marks the endurance: they bear hard things gladly. Without that comma the words could open verse 12, "with joy giving thanks". Both fit Paul (Philippians 4:4-6).

decisions.choice: a share of the inheritance: the picture of Israel's land given by lot, now applied to God's holy people
decisions.reason: μερίδα ("share") and κλήρου ("lot, portion") belong to the Old Testament language of land divided by lot among Israel's tribes (Joshua 14:1-5). Deuteronomy 10:9 uses the two together of the Levites, whose share was the Lord himself. God has given the Colossians, who were not Israelites, a full share in what he promised his people.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "qualified you"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "us", which matches "rescued us" in verse 13. The SBLGNT reads "you", and it is easier to see why a copyist would change "you" to "us" than the reverse. Either way the Colossians are included.

decisions.choice: "in the light" goes with the inheritance: the holy people's share is in God's realm of light
alternatives: the holy ones who live in the light
decisions.reason: Light is set against "the authority of darkness" in verse 13: two realms with two rulers. In Acts 26:18 Paul is sent to turn people "from darkness to light" so that they may receive a share among those made holy.

decisions.choice: the authority of darkness: the rule of evil that once held them
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Luke 22:53 for the hour of Jesus' arrest. Darkness is pictured as a power with its own rule, like the powers Christ disarmed at the cross (2:15).

decisions.choice: transferred: moved from one realm to another
decisions.reason: μεθίστημι means to move someone from one place or position to another (Acts 13:22 uses it of God removing Saul as king). God has already taken believers out of the dark realm and set them in the Son's kingdom: both verbs tell of something done.

decisions.choice: the Son of his love: his beloved Son
alternatives: the Son who brings his love
decisions.reason: In biblical Greek a noun in the genitive often works like an adjective. God calls Jesus his beloved Son at his baptism (Mark 1:11).

decisions.choice: redemption: release, as of a captive or slave, here explained as the forgiveness of sins
alternatives: the payment of a ransom price
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσιν means setting free, as a slave or captive was set free. Paul explains it at once: the release is the forgiveness of sins (compare Ephesians 1:7). The idea of a price paid is in the background (1 Corinthians 6:20) but is not the point here.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "through his blood"
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "through his blood", taken from the matching words in Ephesians 1:7. The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Colossians speaks of his blood in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the wisdom and understanding the Spirit gives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the wisdom comes from (m3); Literal keeps "spiritual".

decisions.choice: live
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure of speech for the way one lives (m4); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: made you fit
decisions.reason: God himself has made them able to have this share. "Made fit" says so without suggesting an exam they passed.

decisions.choice: your share of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people in the kingdom of light
alternatives: the share of the inheritance of the holy ones in the light
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of an inheritance and of light as a realm (m9, m11).

decisions.choice: Through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son
decisions.reason: Readable names the Son and says what "in him" means here: it is through him that we are set free.

records.heading: Paul's prayer, and the Son above all creation

records.source: ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀοράτου, πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκτίσθη τὰ πάντα ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὰ ὁρατὰ καὶ τὰ ἀόρατα, εἴτε θρόνοι εἴτε κυριότητες εἴτε ἀρχαὶ εἴτε ἐξουσίαι· τὰ πάντα δι’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ἔκτισται·
records.gloss: who is image of the God the invisible, firstborn of all creation, \v 16 because in him were created the all things in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; the all things through him and for him have been created;
pieces: The Son is the image of the unseen God, the firstborn who stands above all creation.

For in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everything in heaven and on earth was created, the seen and the unseen, whether thrones or dominions, rulers or authorities. Everything has been created through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.15: He is [the] image of the invisible God, [the] firstborn of all creation,
L.16: because in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.15: No one can see God, but the Son shows us what God is like. The Son is the firstborn: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has first place over everything God has made.
R.16: For it was by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that God made everything, in heaven and on earth, the things we can see and the things we cannot. That includes every power that rules: thrones and lords, rulers and authorities, in the spiritual world as well as in this one. God made everything through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: who: the Son of God's love (verse 13)
decisions.reason: ὅς continues from verses 13-14, so the subject of verses 15-20 is the Son. These verses have a balanced shape, like a poem or hymn: verses 15-16 praise the Son as the one through whom all things were made, and verses 18-20 as the one through whom all things are made new. Both halves turn on the word πρωτότοκος ("firstborn").

decisions.choice: image: the Son makes the unseen God visible and known
alternatives: image: a mere likeness or copy
decisions.reason: An εἰκὼν is a likeness that shows the one it represents. God cannot be seen (John 1:18; 1 Timothy 1:17), but in the Son he is seen (2 Corinthians 4:4). The word also recalls Genesis 1:26-27, where humans are made in God's image; in Christ that image is shown in full, and believers are being renewed in it (3:10).

decisions.choice: firstborn: the one with the rank and rights of the firstborn, supreme over creation, not the first thing created
alternatives: born before creation, in time only
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament the firstborn son held first place and was heir, and God says of the king he chooses that he will set him as firstborn, high above the kings of the earth (Psalm 89:28). Verse 16 gives the reason for the title: all things were created in him, so he is not one of the created things. The genitive πάσης κτίσεως can mean "of" or "over" all creation; with this sense he stands above it.

decisions.choice: in him: God made all things in the Son and by him
alternatives: in him: within him, as in a place
decisions.reason: ἐν αὐτῷ may name Christ as the means of creation, like "through him" at the end of the verse, or as the one in whom creation has its pattern and meaning. The passive ἐκτίσθη ("were created") leaves God as the creator, acting in the Son (compare John 1:3; Hebrews 1:2).

decisions.choice: thrones, dominions, rulers, authorities: ranks of powers, especially unseen spiritual powers
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of Paul's day named orders of angelic powers, and Paul uses "rulers and authorities" of spiritual powers (2:15; Ephesians 6:12). The list follows "the invisible", so unseen powers are mainly in view, though earthly rulers are not excluded. Whatever powers the Colossians feared or honored (2:18) were made by Christ and for him.

decisions.choice: for him: Christ is the goal of creation, and creation stands as his work
decisions.reason: εἰς αὐτὸν names the purpose for which everything exists. The verb changes from ἐκτίσθη ("were created", the act) to ἔκτισται ("have been created", a perfect), so creation is seen as an act whose results last.

decisions.choice: He (L); The Son (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek continues the sentence of verses 13-14 with "who". Every level starts a new sentence here; Balanced and Readable name the Son so the reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: lordships (L); dominions (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the link with the word for "lord"; Balanced uses the usual English word for the realm of a lord.

decisions.choice: the firstborn who stands above all creation (B); has first place over everything God has made (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the title means here (m3), so that it is not read as "the first thing created".

decisions.choice: No one can see God, but the Son shows us what God is like
alternatives: He is the image of the invisible God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "image" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: every power that rules: thrones and lords, rulers and authorities, in the spiritual world as well as in this one
alternatives: whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities
decisions.reason: Readable says what the four titles are (m5).

records.source: καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν πρὸ πάντων καὶ τὰ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ συνέστηκεν, καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ σώματος τῆς ἐκκλησίας· ὅς ἐστιν ἀρχή, πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, ἵνα γένηται ἐν πᾶσιν αὐτὸς πρωτεύων, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ εὐδόκησεν πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα κατοικῆσαι καὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ ἀποκαταλλάξαι τὰ πάντα εἰς αὐτόν, εἰρηνοποιήσας διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ σταυροῦ αὐτοῦ, δι’ αὐτοῦ εἴτε τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἴτε τὰ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·
records.gloss: and he is before all things and the all things in him hold together, \v 18 and he is the head of the body, the church; who is beginning, firstborn from the dead, so that he may become in all things himself holding first place, \v 19 because in him was pleased all the fullness to dwell \v 20 and through him to reconcile the all things to him, having made peace through the blood of the cross of him, through him, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens;
pieces: He exists before all things, and all things are held together in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
He is also the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the first to be born from among the dead, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would come to hold first place in everything.
For God in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness was pleased to dwell in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to reconcile all things to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, making peace by the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross: all things through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, on earth and in heaven alike.

L.17: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is before all things, and all things hold together in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.18: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the head of the body, the church. He is [the] beginning, [the] firstborn from the dead, so that in all things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} might come to have first place,
L.19: because in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the fullness was pleased to dwell
L.20: and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to reconcile all things to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having made peace through the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross, through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens.

R.17: The Son existed before everything else, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds everything together.
R.18: He is also the head of the church, which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads it and gives it life. He is where God's new creation begins, the first to rise from the dead, never to die again. So in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has first place.
R.19: For God was pleased to live fully in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is,
R.20: and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bring everything back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, everything on earth and everything in heaven. God made peace through the blood {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son poured out when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross.

decisions.choice: he is before all things: before them in time and above them in rank
decisions.reason: αὐτός is emphatic: he himself. The verb is present, ἐστιν ("is", not "was"), which fits one who did not come into being with the rest (compare John 8:58).

decisions.choice: hold together: he keeps the universe in being and in order
decisions.reason: συνίστημι in the perfect means to stand together, to hold together as one whole. The one through whom all was made also keeps it from falling apart (Hebrews 1:3).

decisions.choice: head: the one who rules the body and is the source of its life
alternatives: head: the leading member within the body
decisions.reason: Here the church is Christ's body and he is its head: over it as its ruler, and the source from which it grows (2:19; Ephesians 4:15-16). In 1 Corinthians 12:21 Paul uses the picture differently, with the head as one member among others. τῆς ἐκκλησίας explains σώματος: the body is the church.

decisions.choice: beginning: the origin and first of God's new creation
alternatives: the beginning of the first creation
decisions.reason: ἀρχή can mean "beginning" or "ruler" (the plural means "rulers" in verse 16). Here it is joined to "firstborn from the dead", so it is the start of the new creation that his resurrection begins (1 Corinthians 15:20-23).

decisions.choice: firstborn from the dead: the first to rise to a life that never ends, ahead of all who will follow
decisions.reason: Others were raised before Jesus, but they died again. He is the first to rise from the dead to new, lasting life, and the first of many (1 Corinthians 15:20; Revelation 1:5). The word πρωτότοκος repeats verse 15: he is first over the old creation and first in the new.

decisions.choice: so that in everything he might come to hold first place
decisions.reason: πᾶσιν can be neuter ("in everything") or masculine ("among all"). With "all things" repeated through these verses, the neuter fits best. The verb γένηται ("might become") says that by his resurrection he came to hold the first place that verses 15-17 say was his.

decisions.choice: the fullness is God himself: God in all his fullness was pleased to dwell in the Son
alternatives: God was pleased to have all the fullness dwell in him
the fullness is a power or being of its own
decisions.reason: πλήρωμα is neuter, but the participle εἰρηνοποιήσας ("having made peace") in verse 20 is masculine, so the one who was pleased and who made peace is a person: God. 2:9 says the same thing outright: all the fullness of deity dwells in Christ bodily.

decisions.choice: dwell: settle for good, make one's home
alternatives: visit or stay for a while
decisions.reason: κατοικέω means to live in a place permanently, not as a passing guest. In 2:9 the same verb is in the present: the fullness dwells in him now.

decisions.choice: to himself: to God
alternatives: to him: to Christ, as the goal of all things (verse 16)
decisions.reason: αὐτόν could point to Christ, since verse 16 says all things were made "for him". But reconciling is God's work through Christ (2 Corinthians 5:18-19), and God is the one who was pleased in verse 19, so "to himself" is more likely.

decisions.choice: reconcile all things: bring the whole creation, on earth and in heaven, back into peace and right order under God
alternatives: every person and every power will in the end be saved
decisions.reason: Peace is made by the cross. For people, being reconciled means being brought back to God, and continuing in faith (verses 21-23). For the hostile powers, the letter speaks of their being disarmed and led in triumph (2:15). Paul does not say here how each part of creation is reconciled.

decisions.choice: the blood of his cross: Christ's violent death, given as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Blood stands for a life given up in death, and in the Old Testament the blood of sacrifice makes atonement (Leviticus 17:11). God makes peace through Jesus' death on a Roman cross, the most shameful of deaths.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: keep the second "through him"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts do not have the repeated "through him". If it is original, it stresses once more that all reconciliation comes through Christ. The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: God in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness was pleased (B); God was pleased to live fully in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
alternatives: all the fullness was pleased to dwell
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject (m7); Literal keeps "all the fullness".

decisions.choice: the head of the church, which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads it and gives it life
alternatives: the head of the body, the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what "head" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: where God's new creation begins, the first to rise from the dead, never to die again
alternatives: the beginning, the firstborn from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two titles (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: bring everything back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: "Reconcile" is not an everyday word for many readers; Readable says what it means, here and in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the blood {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son poured out when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the blood of his cross" refers to (m11).

records.source: καὶ ὑμᾶς ποτε ὄντας ἀπηλλοτριωμένους καὶ ἐχθροὺς τῇ διανοίᾳ ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς πονηροῖς νυνὶ δὲ ἀποκατηλλάγητε ἐν τῷ σώματι τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου παραστῆσαι ὑμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους καὶ ἀνεγκλήτους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ, εἴ γε ἐπιμένετε τῇ πίστει τεθεμελιωμένοι καὶ ἑδραῖοι καὶ μὴ μετακινούμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὗ ἠκούσατε, τοῦ κηρυχθέντος ἐν πάσῃ κτίσει τῇ ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν, οὗ ἐγενόμην ἐγὼ Παῦλος διάκονος.
records.gloss: And you once being alienated and hostile in the mind in the works the evil, \v 22 now but you were reconciled in the body of the flesh of him through the death, to present you holy and unblemished and irreproachable before him, \v 23 if indeed you continue in the faith, having been founded and firm and not being shifted away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, the [one] having been proclaimed in all creation the [one] under the heaven, of which became I Paul servant.
pieces: Once you were estranged from God, hostile to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in your thinking, as your evil deeds showed.

But now you have been reconciled by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s death in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} physical body, so that God may bring you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence holy, without blemish, and free from any charge,

provided that you stay in the faith, firm on your foundation and steady, not drifting away from the hope held out in the gospel you heard. This gospel has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and I, Paul, have become its servant.

L.21: And you, who were once alienated and hostile in mind in evil deeds,
L.22: but now you have been reconciled in the body of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh through the death, to present you holy and unblemished and beyond reproach before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.23: if indeed you continue in the faith, founded and firm and not being moved away from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which has been proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a servant.

R.21: There was a time when you were far from God. In your minds you were {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, and the evil things you did showed it.
R.22: But now God has brought you back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through the death of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body. God did this so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can bring you before {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} holy, with no fault in you and nothing anyone can accuse you of.
R.23: But you must hold on to your faith. Stand firm on it, like a house on a solid foundation, and do not let anything move you away from the hope that the good news gives you. You have heard this good news, and it has been told all over the world. I, Paul, have become a servant of this good news.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you have been reconciled"
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts have the active ἀποκαταλλάσσω, "he reconciled", which fits the "you" that begins the sentence as an object. The SBLGNT follows a few early manuscripts with the passive, which leaves that opening "you" without its verb. Copyists were more likely to smooth such a break than to create it. Either way God is the one who reconciles (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: the sentence begins with "you" as an object, then breaks off and starts again: "but now you have been reconciled"
decisions.reason: Verse 21 sets out what they once were, and verse 22 breaks off and restarts with νυνὶ δὲ ("but now"). The break makes the contrast sharp: once, but now.

decisions.choice: alienated: cut off from God, and hostile to him
decisions.reason: ἀπαλλοτριόομαι means to be made a stranger, shut out. Ephesians uses the same word for Gentiles shut out from God's people and from the life of God (Ephesians 2:12; 4:18). The hostility is toward God, as in Romans 5:10.

decisions.choice: hostile in their thinking, which showed in evil deeds
decisions.reason: διανοίᾳ says where the hostility lived: in their minds. ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς πονηροῖς says where it showed: in what they did.

decisions.choice: the body of his flesh: his real, physical body
decisions.reason: The doubled phrase stresses that reconciliation happened in Christ's actual human body, through his death, and sets it apart from "the body" that is the church in verse 18. It may also answer teaching that treated the body with contempt (2:23).

decisions.choice: God presents them before himself, holy and blameless
alternatives: Christ presents them before himself (as in Ephesians 5:27)
decisions.reason: The subject of παραστῆσαι ("to present") is not named. Since God is the one who reconciles (verses 19-20), he is most likely the one who presents them, before himself (compare Ephesians 1:4, where God chose his people to be holy and without fault in his sight). In Ephesians 5:27 Christ presents the church to himself, so that reading is possible.

decisions.choice: words from sacrifice and the law court
decisions.reason: ἀμώμους is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for sacrificial animals without defect (Exodus 29:1), and ἀνεγκλήτους means that no charge can be brought (1 Corinthians 1:8). They will stand before God like a perfect offering, with no accusation against them.

decisions.choice: if indeed: a real condition, stated with confidence
decisions.reason: εἴ γε ("if indeed") makes their continuing a true condition of being presented holy. Yet Paul says it with confidence, as in 2:5-7: he is urging them on, not doubting them.

decisions.choice: faith: their trust in Christ
alternatives: the faith: the body of Christian teaching
decisions.reason: πίστει has the article, which can point either way. With "the hope of the gospel" alongside, it is their own continuing trust that is in view, though trust and the teaching it holds to cannot be separated (2:7).

decisions.choice: a building picture: founded, firm, not shifted
decisions.reason: θεμελιόω is used of a building set on its foundation, ἑδραῖοι means seated firmly and steady, and μετακινέω means to be moved from one's place. They are to stay where the gospel has set them.

decisions.choice: proclaimed in all creation under heaven: spread far and wide
decisions.reason: The phrase is a way of saying "everywhere", like "in all the world" in verse 6. The gospel had spread across the Roman world in Paul's day (Romans 1:8; 10:18), not to every individual.

decisions.choice: servant of the gospel
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, διάκονος means one who serves. Paul serves the gospel here, and the church in verse 25.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s death in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} physical body (B); the death of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body (R)
alternatives: in the body of his flesh through the death
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Christ, since "his" after "you have been reconciled" could be unclear. "Physical" and "human" say what "the body of his flesh" means (m5).

decisions.choice: hostile to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; God may bring you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence
alternatives: hostile in mind; to present you before him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God where the Greek leaves him to be understood (m3, m6).

decisions.choice: God has brought you back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, Readable says what "reconcile" means, and names God as the one who does it, as the passive implies (m1).

decisions.choice: like a house on a solid foundation
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the building picture (m10).

decisions.choice: to every creature under heaven (B); all over the world (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means "everywhere" (m11). Balanced keeps its form; Readable says what it means.

records.source: Νῦν χαίρω ἐν τοῖς παθήμασιν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, καὶ ἀνταναπληρῶ τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου ὑπὲρ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ, ὅ ἐστιν ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἧς ἐγενόμην ἐγὼ διάκονος κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι εἰς ὑμᾶς πληρῶσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ μυστήριον τὸ ἀποκεκρυμμένον ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν γενεῶν, νῦν δὲ ἐφανερώθη τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ, οἷς ἠθέλησεν ὁ θεὸς γνωρίσαι τί τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τοῦ μυστηρίου τούτου ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, ὅ ἐστιν Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς δόξης·
records.gloss: Now I rejoice in the sufferings on behalf of you, and I fill up in turn the lacking things of the afflictions of the Christ in the flesh of me on behalf of the body of him, which is the church, \v 25 of which became I servant according to the stewardship of the God the [one] having been given to me for you, to fulfill the word of the God, \v 26 the mystery the [one] having been hidden from the ages and from the generations, now but was revealed to the holy [ones] of him, \v 27 to whom willed the God to make known what [is] the riches of the glory of the mystery this among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of the glory;
pieces: Now I am glad to suffer for your sake. In my own body I am completing what is still lacking in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s afflictions, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, the church.
I became its servant by the task God gave me for your benefit: to make the word of God fully known,
the mystery that was kept hidden through all past ages and generations but has now been revealed to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people.
God chose to make known to them how rich and glorious this mystery is among the Gentiles. The mystery is this: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in you, the hope of glory.

L.24: Now I rejoice in [my] sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up in turn what is lacking of the afflictions of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, which is the church,
L.25: of which I became a servant according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
L.26: the mystery that has been hidden from the ages and from the generations, but now was revealed to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones,
L.27: to whom God willed to make known what [is] the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in you, the hope of glory.

R.24: I am glad to suffer for you now. In my own body I am going through the troubles that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s people must still suffer for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I suffer them for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, which is the church.
R.25: God gave me the work of serving the church, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave it to me for your good, so that I would tell you the whole message of God.
R.26: This message is a mystery: God's plan, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept hidden for ages, through all the generations of the past. But now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown it to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people.
R.27: God wanted them to know how rich and glorious this mystery is for people who are not Jews. Here is the mystery: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lives in you! So you can be sure that you will share in God's glory.

decisions.choice: Paul rejoices in the sufferings he bears for their sake
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ("for you") says his sufferings are for their good: he is a prisoner for the gospel that reached them (4:3, 4:18).

decisions.choice: what is lacking in Christ's afflictions: the sufferings still to be borne by Christ's people, which Christ counts as his own; nothing is lacking in his saving death
alternatives: Christ's death was not enough, and Paul's suffering completes it
decisions.reason: The letter has just said that God made peace through the blood of the cross (verses 20-22), so nothing is missing there. θλῖψις is never used in the New Testament for Christ's atoning death; it means hardships and troubles. Christ is so joined to his people that their sufferings are his (Acts 9:4; 2 Corinthians 1:5; Philippians 3:10), and there is a share of suffering still to come, which Paul gladly takes up "in my flesh" for the church. The exact sense is debated.

decisions.choice: fill up in turn: Paul does his part
decisions.reason: ἀνταναπληρῶ adds to the verb "fill up" a prefix meaning "in turn" or "in return": Paul takes up his own share of what remains.

decisions.choice: stewardship: a task God entrusted to Paul, like a household manager's charge
alternatives: God's plan or arrangement (as in Ephesians 1:10)
decisions.reason: οἰκονομίαν is the work of a steward who manages a household for its master (Luke 16:2-4). Paul speaks of his commission the same way in 1 Corinthians 4:1-2 and 9:17. It was given to him "for you", for the sake of Gentiles like the Colossians.

decisions.choice: to fulfill the word of God: to proclaim it fully, carrying it as far as it is meant to go
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same verb in Romans 15:19 for having fully proclaimed the gospel from Jerusalem to Illyricum. Preaching to the Gentiles brings God's word to its full reach.

decisions.choice: mystery: a secret of God's purpose, hidden until he reveals it
alternatives: secret rites known only to members, as in the mystery cults
decisions.reason: In the Bible, μυστήριον is a secret that only God can disclose (Daniel 2:28), and Paul uses it for God's plan now made known in Christ (Romans 16:25-26; Ephesians 3:3-6). It is not a puzzle, and it is not kept for a few: it has been revealed to his holy people and is proclaimed to everyone (verse 28).

decisions.choice: hidden for ages and generations: through all past time
alternatives: hidden from the "ages" as spiritual powers
decisions.reason: αἰώνων and γενεῶν are words of time here: the secret was hidden through all earlier ages and from all earlier generations of people, and νῦν ("now") marks the change.

decisions.choice: the sentence changes its construction: "hidden ... but now revealed"
decisions.reason: The participle "having been hidden" is followed by a main verb, ἐφανερώθη ("was revealed"). The break brings "now" to the front, as in verse 22.

decisions.choice: among the Gentiles: the peoples other than Israel
decisions.reason: ἔθνεσιν means the nations, and in Jewish use the peoples other than Israel. The Colossians were mostly Gentiles (1:21; 2:13). That God's Messiah lives among and within such people is the heart of the secret.

decisions.choice: Christ in you: Christ living in each of them and among them as a church
alternatives: Christ among you Gentiles, as a group only
decisions.reason: ὑμῖν is plural, so it can mean "among you" or "within you". The phrase just before ("among the Gentiles") suggests "among"; "the hope of glory" suggests Christ living within each believer (Romans 8:10). The two do not exclude each other.

decisions.choice: the hope of glory: the sure expectation of sharing God's glory when Christ appears
decisions.reason: Christ in them now is the pledge that they will share his glory when he appears (3:4).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article in verse 24.

decisions.choice: the troubles that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s people must still suffer for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
alternatives: what is lacking in Christ's afflictions
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m2, which is uncertain.

decisions.choice: the task God gave me (B); God gave me the work (R)
decisions.reason: The plain sense of the household word (m4).

decisions.choice: mystery: God's plan, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept hidden
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "mystery", as Literal and Balanced do and as Ephesians does at every level, so the word stays the same wherever Paul uses it. Because in current English "mystery" can suggest a puzzle, Readable says at once what this mystery is: God's plan, once hidden and now made known (m6).

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles" (m9).

records.heading: Paul toils to make the mystery known

records.source: ὃν ἡμεῖς καταγγέλλομεν νουθετοῦντες πάντα ἄνθρωπον καὶ διδάσκοντες πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ, ἵνα παραστήσωμεν πάντα ἄνθρωπον τέλειον ἐν Χριστῷ·
records.gloss: whom we proclaim, warning every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, so that we may present every man complete in Christ;
pieces: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is the one we proclaim. We warn {{gender:every person|every man}} and teach {{gender:every person|every man}} with all wisdom, so that we may bring {{gender:every person|every man}} before God mature in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.28: Him we proclaim, warning every {{gender:person|man}} and teaching every {{gender:person|man}} in all wisdom, so that we may present every {{gender:person|man}} complete in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.28: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is the one we tell people about. We warn and teach {{gender:every person|every man}}, using all the wisdom God gives. We want to bring {{gender:every person|every man}} to God as a mature believer who belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: whom: Christ, named at the end of verse 27
decisions.reason: ὃν picks up "Christ in you". The message Paul proclaims is a person.

decisions.choice: every person, without exception
decisions.reason: πάντα ἄνθρωπον is said three times. The noun means a human being, man or woman. The repetition stresses that the wisdom of the gospel is for every believer, not kept for a few.

decisions.choice: warning and teaching: correcting what is wrong and instructing in what is right
decisions.reason: νουθετέω means to set someone's mind right by warning; διδάσκω is to teach. Believers are to do the same for one another (3:16).

decisions.choice: complete, mature: grown to full stature in Christ, not sinless
decisions.reason: τέλειον describes what has reached its goal: full-grown, complete (1 Corinthians 14:20; Philippians 3:15). The picture is the day when believers are presented to God (compare verse 22).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in Christ"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Jesus". The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: every {{gender:person|man}} (L); {{gender:every person|every man}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, so the default is inclusive; "every man" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the one we proclaim; before God (B), to God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Christ for "whom" and say to whom believers are presented (as in verse 22).

decisions.choice: using all the wisdom God gives
decisions.reason: Readable says where the wisdom comes from (compare verse 9), so that it is not taken for Paul's own cleverness.

records.source: εἰς ὃ καὶ κοπιῶ ἀγωνιζόμενος κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐνεργουμένην ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν δυνάμει.
records.gloss: for which also I toil, struggling according to the working of him, the [one] working in me in power.
pieces: This is the goal I toil for, struggling by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} energy, which is powerfully at work in me.

L.29: For this I also toil, struggling according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} working, which is at work in me in power.

R.29: That is why I work so hard and keep on struggling. But I do it with the energy {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives me: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty power is at work in me.

decisions.choice: for this: to present every person mature in Christ (verse 28)
decisions.reason: εἰς ὃ ("to which") points back to the goal at the end of verse 28.

decisions.choice: toil and struggle: hard labor, like an athlete straining in a contest
decisions.reason: κοπιάω is work to the point of weariness. ἀγωνίζομαι is the word for competing in the games, and Paul goes on with the related noun in 2:1. His struggle includes prayer (compare 4:12) and imprisonment (4:18).

decisions.choice: his working: the working of Christ, named in verse 28
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to Christ, the last person named. In 2:12 the same word is used for the working of God, who raised Christ; the power is God's, at work through Christ.

decisions.choice: a play on words: the working that works in me
decisions.reason: ἐνέργειαν and ἐνεργουμένην come from the same root, as if "his energy energizing in me". The form ἐνεργουμένην means it is at work by its own power. Paul's effort is real, but the power is not his own.

decisions.choice: the energy {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives me
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ for "his" (m3).

decisions.choice: energy
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of power at work; Literal keeps "working" to show the play on words (m4).
